# RealOrAI: Detecting AI-Generated Images with an ANN

A fully connected Artificial Neural Network (Keras) that classifies an image as a
**REAL** photo or **FAKE** (AI-generated by Stable Diffusion).

## Results (20,000 unseen test images)
| Metric | Score |
|---|---|
| Accuracy | **82.42%** |
| Precision (macro) | 82.45% |
| Recall (macro) | 82.41% |
| F1-score (macro) | 82.41% |

See `results/training_curves.png` and `results/confusion_matrix.png`.

## Model
Input (32×32×3 = 3072 pixels, scaled 0–1) → Dense 512 (ReLU) + BatchNorm + Dropout 0.3
→ Dense 256 (ReLU) + BatchNorm + Dropout 0.3 → Dense 128 (ReLU) + Dropout 0.2
→ Dense 1 (Sigmoid). Adam optimizer (lr 0.001), binary cross-entropy loss,
EarlyStopping and ReduceLROnPlateau.

## Dataset
CIFAKE: 100,000 training images and 20,000 test images, half real and half AI-generated.
https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/birdy654/cifake-real-and-ai-generated-synthetic-images

> J. J. Bird and A. Lotfi, "CIFAKE: Image Classification and Explainable Identification
> of AI-Generated Synthetic Images," IEEE Access, 2024.

Download it and place it so the folders look like this:
```
data/train/REAL   data/train/FAKE
data/test/REAL    data/test/FAKE
```
Or download it with Python:
```python
import kagglehub, shutil
p = kagglehub.dataset_download("birdy654/cifake-real-and-ai-generated-synthetic-images")
shutil.copytree(p, "data", dirs_exist_ok=True)
```

## How to run
```
pip install -r requirements.txt
python data.py        # reads the images once and caches them
python train.py       # trains the model, saves results/realorai_ann.keras + curves
python evaluate.py    # test-set metrics + confusion matrix
python predict.py my_image.jpg
```
A trained model is already included in `results/`, so `predict.py` works straight away.

## Files
| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `data.py` | Loading, normalization, flattening, train/validation split |
| `model.py` | The ANN architecture |
| `train.py` | Training, saves model, history and curves |
| `evaluate.py` | Accuracy, precision, recall, F1, confusion matrix |
| `predict.py` | Predict REAL/FAKE for any image |
